name: Nebruz
tagline: Fugitive stilt-village in the swamp, where justice is swift and the alligators are fed twice a day.

population.mix: Fugitives, escaped slaves, failed merchants, desperate adventurers. Mostly men; few children.
population.demographics: Predominantly human. Heavily male (~4:1). Fewer than a dozen children. Mature adults; young leave, old do not survive.

ruler: Phaid Torngrasp, the Marsh-Hand: elected mayor and magistrate.
faiths: None in public; the temple is shuttered by the Marsh-Hand's decree.
strangers: Called dryboots, and at a disadvantage before the Marsh-Hand.
equipment: No posted prices at Swamp Rat Provisions; everything is haggled.

far: watchtowers on 20′ posts in a half-ring
witch's beard hanging from the trees

dawn: the fish house buying the catch

spring: alligators mating; keep off the edges

situations.name: Sermoner Peryl returns
descriptors: a small boat at the landing

situations.name: An execution
descriptors: the whole village at the alligator pit

itself.title: Swift justice
itself.text: There are no long trials and no prisons. The Marsh-Hand judges, and death sentences end at the alligator pit. Dryboots are at a disadvantage in any dispute.

itself.title: The murkwatch
itself.text: Every able-bodied adult serves 2 shifts a month on watch, chosen by lottery, and failing to serve is a fineable offence.

itself.title: Peace with the swamp
itself.text: A non-aggression treaty with the lizard-men holds, and their burial mounds are inviolable. The froggish-folk, governed by the lizard-men, trade mead and honeycomb.

itself.title: Smugglers' hub
itself.text: Smuggling and private deals are the real trade. The warehouse keepers are underpaid and take bribes.

day: **Gerum o' the Spike** feeds the alligators while a crowd pays 1sp to watch.
**Dandal the Shaver** haggles a stranger to exhaustion.
A froggish-folk trader poles in with mead and honeycomb.
A **venomous snake** lies across the boardwalk; locals step over it.
**2 enforcers** march a manacled dryboot to the Marsh-Hand.
**Kalo the Mad** begs at the fish house door.
night: Screams from the swamp, and nobody looks up.
A boat ties up at the warehouses without lights.
**1d4 giant river rats** nose through the rubbish under the boardwalk.
The ship's bell rings at the Painted Frog, and enforcers run across the street.
Nobody crosses the Punishment Post plaza after dark.

response.watch: 10 enforcers in ring mail with cudgels and short swords, under the Sentinel.
response.arrival_day: 1–2 patrolling enforcers within 1d6 minutes; the gong outside the Enforcers' Post summons the rest.
response.arrival_night: As by day. The ship's bell at the Painted Frog brings enforcers from across the street.
response.reinforcements: The murkwatch and an armed populace, who fight guerrilla-style from the swamp if overwhelmed.
response.strength: Never a garrison and never quiet. Everyone here fights, because everyone here has run from something.

locations.name: Nebruz Harbor
locations.look: A muddy riverbank ringed by wooden quays, shallow from silt.

labels.passage: Docking 1sp a day for a skiff, 5sp per 10′ of length for larger boats, which moor at pilings and send cargo ashore by jollyboat.

locations.name: The Painted Frog
locations.look: A three-storey inn with a crude frog statue at the door.

labels.common_room: Curtained booths, often used for clandestine meetings. A ship's bell by the bar summons the enforcers.
labels.services: Common room 5cp a night; private room 1gp; meals 2cp–1gp; drinks 1cp–2gp. Specialty: mushroom-stuffed eel on wild rice.

locations.name: Mother's Boarding House
locations.look: A hulking three-storey brick building for transient labourers.

labels.services: 5sp a week: cot, blanket, footlocker, and gruel and hard bread twice a day.

locations.name: Enforcers' Post
locations.look: A squat brick building with an iron gong outside.

labels.interior: An armory of 2 spare ring mail, cudgels, and 4 short swords, and a small holding cell.
labels.staff: 1 enforcer always on duty, 1–2 on patrol; the gong summons the rest.

locations.name: Alligator Pit
locations.look: A 30′ × 20′ water pit behind a 4′ fence, holding 4 female alligators of about 11′.

labels.fees: Public feedings twice a day, 1sp to watch. Death sentences end here, by plank at spear-point.

locations.name: Swamp Rat Provisions
locations.hidden: A locked warehouse outbuilding behind the store.

locations.name: The Bloated Leech
locations.look: A low-roofed tavern, dim and open-plan, with a plank-and-barrel bar.

labels.services: Dreg beer 1cp. Bog water 2gp a bottle: a fiery liquor from swamp tubers with a dead leech in each bottle, lucky if swallowed.

locations.name: Punishment Post
locations.look: An 8′ denuded tree trunk in an earthen plaza that doubles as the village green.

labels.custom: Site of corporal punishment. Avoided after dark, because the executed are said to haunt it.

labels.wares: Space rented to river traders for goods in transit.
labels.off_the_books: One underpaid keeper each, open to bribes and regularly used by smugglers.

locations.name: Fish House
locations.look: Buys the catch daily and salts, smokes, and packs it in the back.

labels.prices: Pays well for exotic catches: giant crayfish, swamp eels, giant crabs.

locations.name: Meat & Skins
locations.look: A butchery and tannery, with a smokehouse and stretching room at the back.

labels.wares: Meat, hides, and small leather goods.
labels.prices: Best prices for exotic hides: alligator, snake, swamp beasts.

locations.name: Sundries
locations.look: A shop signed in Common and Gnomish.

labels.wares: Dried herbs, pipeweed, exotic fungi, snake-oil medicines. Buys curiosities from adventurers.
labels.off_the_books: Narcotics, poisons, thieves' tools, and magical components: the worst-kept secret in Nebruz.

locations.name: Dorota's Cottage
locations.look: A small house on the outskirts, closer to the swamp than the boardwalks.

labels.inhabitants: Dorota, the village healer and wise woman since the temple closed.

locations.name: Shuttered Temple
locations.look: A converted storehouse, closed by the Marsh-Hand's decree.

labels.interior: Empty; the furnishings are in warehouse storage.
labels.populace: A small congregation, every two weeks, when Sermoner Peryl returns.

locations.name: Arms & Iron
locations.look: The only stone building in Nebruz.

labels.wares: Ironwork, weapons, arrowheads, and ring and chain mail from bog iron.
labels.prices: Excellent work, held back by low-grade ore.

locations.name: Marsh-Hand's Residence
locations.look: A two-storey building that serves as village hall and Phaid's home.

labels.interior: Civic business on the ground floor; private chambers above.
labels.staff: Phaid is present 75% of the time by day, rarely after dark.

labels.inhabitants: Kalo the Mad, who will not go out after dark.

trouble: The renegade lizard-folk band that maimed Kalo is still loose in the swamp.
The temple's closure still divides the village, and Sermoner Peryl keeps coming back.

neighbors.notes: 3 miles on foot through lizard-man swamp, then 6 miles by boat through the channels.

economy.secondary: Smuggling hub; private criminal and political dealings.
economy.notable: Honey and mead trade with the froggish-folk. Exotic herb market for alchemists and sorcerers.

dm_notes.notes: Effemi Nuha's class_level (MU9) is a concealed identity — she presents as a simple smith. Dorota knows the truth; Effemi does not know Dorota knows. Wilem Stonenose is hiding from a former thieves' guild and will not respond to Thieves' Cant. Sermoner Peryl's small congregation is unnamed. The renegade lizard-folk band that mutilated Kalo is distinct from the treaty tribes to the northwest and is still at large in the swamp.

session_history.notes: Party overnighted in Nebruz en route from Caelrun to Leeandra's hut. No encounters detailed.

marsh_hand.name: Phaid Torngrasp
marsh_hand.title: Marsh-Hand
marsh_hand.role: Combined mayor and magistrate. Elected by popular support. Holds court at his residence; no formal village hall.

sentinel.title: Sentinel
sentinel.role: Sheriff and captain of watch. Commands 10 enforcers.

enforcers.equipment: Ring mail, cudgels, short swords, manacles.

government.law: Swift justice; no prolonged trials or incarceration. Dryboots structurally disadvantaged before the Marsh-Hand.

associated_npcs.name: Leeandra
associated_npcs.role: Swamp priestess; lizard-man diplomatic keystone for the Luric marches
associated_npcs.location: Swamp, several hours southwest of Nebruz

location.description: Western bank of the river through the swamp; accessible via the Caelrun swamp path.

physical.construction: Wood pilings over mud; a few buildings on dry hummocks. Brick for sturdier structures. Reed-thatched roofs. Boardwalks average 3 ft above ground; rush brands and coal braziers after dark.
physical.atmosphere: Grey-green moss on blackened timbers. Witch's beard in the trees. Tea-brown water. Frogs, and screams from the swamp after nightfall.

defenses.natural: Swamp terrain on landward side. Quicksand fields ring the village.
defenses.constructed: 12 watchtowers on 20-ft posts in a semi-circle. Spiked pits and deadfalls in the swamp approaches.
defenses.murkwatch: Every able-bodied adult serves 2 shifts/month by lottery. Failure is a fineable offense.
defenses.militia: Armed populace; veteran warriors and a few magic-users. Guerilla tactics if overwhelmed.

allies.basis: inherently unthreatening and governed by lizard-men; active mead and honeycomb trade
